Date: 2026-07-14
Time: 14:00 - 14:48 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Dr. Raj Patel (CTO - Archon), Emily Tran (Lead ML Eng - Archon), Carlos Rivera (Infra - Archon), Nina Lee (Security - Archon), Jordan Kim (Product - Archon)
summary: Discovery focused on Archon Health's need for dedicated GPU capacity for PHI-sensitive clinical summarization and triage models. Key topics: isolation (VPC/on-prem vs dedicated hosted), burst handling and burst credits, autoscaling expectations, SLA/latency targets, encryption/KMS and HIPAA compliance. Agreement to run a week-long dedicated POC to benchmark p95 latency and throughput; Redwood to send pricing and security artifacts.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll just do intros quick then jump into your current infra and goals. uh Raj, do you want to kick off?
[00:12] Dr. Raj (Archon): sure yeah thanks maya. so Archon is building a clinical triage assistant, we run sensitive patient notes, PHI, obviously HIPAA concerns. primary question: can we get reserved GPUs that are isolated from other tenants and still have bursting when needed?
[00:28] Maya: mm-hmm that's exactly what dedicated is for. liam, want to give a quick overview of dedicated capacity and burst options?
[00:35] Liam (Redwood SE): yeah thanks. so dedicated gives you a reserved GPU pool for predictable throughput and isolation. you can run inside a VPC or we can do a private deployment if you need full air-gapped. bursting is supported via optional burst capacity - think of it as a controlled credit-based burst lane that kicks in when your reserved pool is saturated. some nuances re: cold starts and K-V cache priming though.
[01:05] Emily (Archon): can you explain the KV cache thing? i heard on another call it was a problem for our warm-up times.
[01:12] Liam: sure. the KV cache holds key/value past tokens for generation. when you scale up new nodes they don't have the primed cache so first requests hit p99 higher; to mitigate we do async pre-warm and cross-node caching, plus you can reserve a small headroom in pool to absorb spikes. oftentimes we've seen p95 stable once cache warms. sometimes transcripts will say K-V cash in the auto-transcribe, so ignore that haha.
[01:38] Carlos (Archon Infra): what about multi-tenancy isolation? we cannot have any co-tenant models processing PHI.
[01:44] Maya: understood. dedicated capacity with VPC peering or private control plane gives dedicated hardware — no co-tenancy at the GPU level. for extra assurance we can do dedicated nodes in your VPC or an on-prem bundle if you require physical control.
[01:58] Nina (Security): what about cryptographic boundaries and KMS? we need customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) and audit logs for every inference.
[02:07] Liam: we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, or bring-your-own HSM). audit logs are available via our console and pushed to your SIEM; we can provide the retention options. we'll add the details to the security doc.
[02:21] Jordan (Product): our throughput pattern is pretty spiky — 5x baseline during morning batch ingest windows, spikes last 10-20 minutes. are you recommending fixed reserved GPUs or burst pool only?
[02:31] Liam: good question. typical approach is a base reserved pool sized for steady-state, plus a burst pool sized for expected spike headroom. autoscaling policies can be configured to prefer latency SLOs (scale faster) or cost (prefer queueing). for something like 5x brief spikes, reserved+burst tends to be more reliable for p95.
[02:51] Dr. Raj: target p95 is 250ms for short prompts, p95 800ms for longer clinical summaries. we also want throughput to handle about 80 concurrent inference streams at peak.
[03:01] Maya: okay that's helpful. can you send a sample load profile and example prompt lengths? we'll map to GPU SKU recommendations.
[03:07] Emily: yeah we'll share that, it's on our side.
[03:10] (pause)
[03:16] Maya: procurement question — what lock-in / contract length are we looking at for dedicated? monthly or annual reserved?
[03:22] Liam: we support monthly reserved capacity and annual commitments. annual gives a cost discount and guaranteed capacity. we can also do a short-term pilot where you commit to a week of dedicated capacity for benchmarking before bigger commitment.
[03:35] Carlos: curious about upgrades — if we change model sizes or move to quantized models, how disruptive is that to the pool?
[03:43] Liam: we support mixed-model pools and model pinning for safe rollouts. runtime supports different kernel paths; switching a model may require rolling restarts for some nodes but you can pin specific nodes to certain model variants. also we recommend using versioned endpoints and can do canary rollouts.
[03:58] Nina: compliance — SOC 2 is table stakes, but we need HIPAA attestation and data residency controls. do you have a HIPAA BAAs?
[04:07] Maya: yes we have HIPAA BAA offerings for Dedicated and Private customers; RH can sign BAA. we'll attach the SOC 2 report and HIPAA FAQ.
[04:15] Dr. Raj: what about encryption in transit and at rest? logs?
[04:19] Liam: HTTPS/TLS for in transit, at-rest encryption with customer-managed KMS. audit logs are tamper-evident; we can push them to your log storage for long-term retention.
[04:29] Jordan: any limits on model size? we're evaluating a 70B open model and also smaller 13B models quantized.
[04:35] Liam: we support up to 70B reasonably on certain GPU SKUs; quantized 13B runs very efficiently and can reduce cost substantially. (auto-transcript sometimes flips '13-B' to '13P' so apologies).
[04:49] Maya: competitor question — you mentioned OpenAI for hosted and Anthropic earlier; how do you position Redwood for enterprise dedicated vs them?
[04:57] Liam: openai is great for hosted simple use cases; for dedicated enterprise with isolation, on-prem, and cost control Redwood gives more configuration and predictable economics. Anthropic offers models but not the same infra control we provide for private deployments.
[05:12] Emily: networking — if we go VPC peering, what's the egress pattern? do requests route through Redwood control plane?
[05:18] Liam: we offer two models: peered VPC where data stays in your network to model nodes and control plane connections are limited, or a private control plane where we minimize egress and you manage data plane. we'll include topology diagrams.
[05:30] Dr. Raj: okay, so next steps for us are to run a short POC. we'd like to test p95 latency at our peak burst profile and verify isolation and audit logs. can you also provide pricing for monthly reserved 8xA100 equiv and burst to 16 for short periods?
[05:45] Maya: yes — we'll size based on your load profile. liam will propose topology and autoscale policy; i'll include pricing tiers for monthly vs annual reserved.
[05:53] Carlos: who will own the initial setup? devops on our side or do you offer setup assistance?
[05:58] Maya: Redwood has an onboarding team to run the initial provisioning and can do co-managed setup. for private/on-prem there's an ops engagement fee. we'll put that in the quote.
[06:07] Nina: auditability — can you show a sample audit log entry?
[06:11] Liam: yes, we'll attach an example from a previous customer (redacted).
[06:15] Jordan: timeline — if we greenlight pilot next week, how soon could we spin up a dedicated cluster?
[06:20] Liam: for hosted dedicated in our public regions, we can usually provision within 2-5 business days; private or on-prem will take longer, typically 3-6 weeks depending on network approvals.
[06:32] (brief cross-talk)
[06:36] Maya: all right wrapping up. recap: Redwood to send pricing, security docs (SOC2, HIPAA, KMS guide), topology recommendations, and propose POC dates. Archon to send load profile and security questionnaire.
[06:50] Dr. Raj: sounds good. any blockers from procurement side we should pre-empt?
[06:54] Maya: procurement will want standard IP/usage terms, BAA, and SLAs. i'll include standard language and we can iterate.
[07:02] Emily: one more technical — can we run model evals on small sample data locally to validate outputs before POC?
[07:08] Liam: yes you can run local evals or we can provision a small dedicated dev pool. either works.
[07:14] Maya: i'll follow up with the action items, thanks everyone.
[07:18] (meeting ends)

Notes: auto-transcription had intermittent errors (KV cash, 13P). There was some crosstalk during sizing discussion. Action items and next steps captured above.
